newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta's bank chief worried about credit level.
newsitem.headline: Malta's bank chief worried about credit level.

text.p: Malta's Central Bank governor warned at the weekend that credit to the government had increased by an "unacceptably high" 24 percent during the 12 months to last October.

"If unchecked (this) could lead to a serious economic imbalance. There is a risk that the public sector may take up too great a portion of the financial resources available, thus leading to overcrowding," governor Francis J. Vassallo said.
"In such a situation the private sector could find difficulty in financing its own activity," he told a dinner of the Chartered Institute of Bankers.
Vassallo gave no figures but stressed that the government, elected in October, should reduce its borrowing requirements to more acceptable levels.
"I have no doubt that the new finance minister is equally concerned...I hope he will set a targeted programme to reduce the deficit...without creating undue economic pressures."
Figures issued by the Central Bank up to June showed government debt at Lm459.3 million ($1,286 million), up by Lm86.3 million from June 1995. All the increase took the form of local borrowing.
Vassallo said monetary policy had to be tightened "otherwise we will pay an unacceptably high price in terms of...long term economic success."
Consumption has remained strong, fuelling imports, and Malta's export performance was not as dynamic as in the past, while tourism arrivals were down this year, commented Vassallo.

"These developments have had an adverse effect on the balance of payments and Malta's external reserves. The currenct account of the balance of payments remains in deficit and this does not seem to have been adequately addressed," he said.

The governor said however that last September the average solvency ratio for credit institutions operating locally was 13 percent compared to the minimum requirement of eight percent under international supervisory standards.
On average, banks' liquid assets amounted to 33 percent of their deposit liabilities.
